statements.t: We anticipate continued strength in our Water Infrastructure segment, with incremental revenue growth expected in the fourth quarter for the base business before including any partial fourth quarter contributions from the recently closed acquisition of Pilot Water.
“We are increasingly excited about the addition of Pilot Water and the additional opportunities it enables, and we expect strong growth in our Water Infrastructure segment as we look ahead.

We continue to win new contracted organic growth projects that underwrite scaled network expansion and we believe our combined infrastructure asset base will provide for incremental, critically needed solutions to help our customers solve the complex water dynamics in the Delaware basin.

“Taking into consideration the divestment and deconsolidation of Peak Rentals and a partial quarter contribution from Pilot Water, we anticipate Adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter growing to an estimated $95 - $100 million.

Additionally, as we begin integrating the combined asset base and finish out Pilot Water’s ongoing capital projects during the fourth quarter, we now anticipate net capital expenditures for 2026 of approximately $300 – $310 million.

We have significantly enhanced our Water Infrastructure business with the acquisition of Pilot Water and continue to add organic project wins that drive more contracted produced water volumes on our system.

Looking ahead, the Company anticipates Water Infrastructure revenues of $150 - $160 million in the fourth quarter of 2026, driven by a partial quarter contribution from Pilot Water, with gross margins before D&A in the 52% – 56% range in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Normalizing for the divestment of Peak Rentals, which contributed approximately 21% of the segment’s revenues year-to-date, the Company anticipates typical fourth quarter seasonality for the segment resulting in mid single-digit percent declines sequentially for the remaining segment.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company anticipates revenues of $75 – $80 million, driven by the timing of key customer activity levels and fourth quarter seasonality, with gross margins before D&A remaining steady in the 17% – 18% range for the segment.
